candidates.text: The right to travel discussed in our cases embraces at least three different components. It protects the right of a citizen of one State to enter and to leave another State
candidates.speaker: Stevens, for the Court
phrases: right to be treated as a welcome visitor rather than an unfriendly alien

candidates.text: Congress has no affirmative power to authorize the States to violate the Fourteenth Amendment and is implicitly prohibited from passing legislation
candidates.speaker: Stevens, for the Court
phrases: Congress has no affirmative power to authorize the States to violate the Fourteenth Amendment

candidates.text: Citizens of the United States, whether rich or poor, have the right to choose to be citizens of the State wherein they reside.
candidates.speaker: Stevens, for the Court
phrases: The States, however, do not have any right to select their citizens

candidates.text: A person is no longer traveling in any sense of the word when he finishes his journey to a State
candidates.speaker: Rehnquist, dissenting
phrases: no longer traveling in any sense of the word

candidates.text: We should also consider whether the Clause should displace, rather than augment, portions of our equal protection
